argument_summary: The certification case is narrower than a claim that rollout controls cured the weakness. The admissible record supports a caveated certification position based on three points taken together: aggregate launch readiness passed, public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk through deployment, and the rollout is limited and reversible. The same record also requires a clear limitation: the affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed, is below target on residency documentation guidance, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that evidence, the supportable packet is certification only on a disclosure-based theory with monitored rollout, not certification on a controls-alone theory.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost evidence is added. From the existing record, a no-escalation path is available if the auditor evaluates certification on the narrower disclosure-plus-monitoring basis rather than rejecting it for lack of a controls-only justification.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating the 7% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring dashboard as sufficient by themselves when the affected use case remains exposed. The admissible policy text instead allows a compliant path here only if the material limitation for the named launch use case is disclosed before launch, unless it was resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Because the available risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not address the exposed public benefits eligibility segment, the defensible certification position is caveated compliance conditioned on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of that limitation.
concessions: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains in the initial rollout cohort.
That segment is below target on residency documentation guidance.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address this exposure.
The current admissible record does not support any claim that rollout controls alone satisfy the policy.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal support general readiness, but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure requirement.
